description.narrative: Study and Research in Africa aims to increase the attractiveness of African higher education offer for all types of mobile learners within Africa and to Africa. It seeks to strengthen regional integration, knowledge networks, cooperation, branding of EU-funded programmes in African Higher Education and in particular support the effective creation of the African Higher Education and Research Space (AHERS). The programme will also support the capacity building of universities/ and their affiliated research centres (RCs)[1] to interact with the wider eco-system (i.e., public and private organizations and institutions, development finance institutions, civil society organizations, etc.) in Global Gateway (GG) investment priority areas such as digital, climate, energy, transport, health, and applied research so that they play a stronger role in the skills development and innovation of value chains and build up a more relevant training offer. It will build scale, connect initiatives, and increase the relevance of projects funded through EU, as well as MS programmes and will offer an enabling facility to build up multilayer partnerships at the country level, increasing the chances of countries to access EFSD+. In the medium term, the Action will support the attractiveness of African Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) by creating a platform to disseminate information, advancing the wider ecosystem of HEIs in Africa and by supporting HEIs access to EU funds.Contributing towards the external dimension of the European Education Area¿s European Universities Strategy, the action will be structured around three components covering Opportunities, Partnerships and Targeted Support, all contributing to a transformational impact of Team Europe efforts in Africa in the field of higher education.The action is part of the Youth Mobility for Africa GG flagship initiative, which brings together several EU programmes in higher education and youth, such as Erasmus+, the Intra-Africa Academic Mobility Scheme and the Africa-EU Youth Academy under one umbrella. Supporting continental integration, providing learning opportunities both within Africa, and between Africa and Europe and reinforcing cooperation to leverage investment in knowledge and innovation to support strategic autonomy and sustainable value chains, build scale and enhance African higher education¿s relevance and responsiveness to labour market needs in partner countries, while also creating green growth, are core elements of the GG Africa-Europe Investment Package and are the aims of the Youth Mobility for Africa GG Flagship Initiative.Concretely, the Action will focus on three specific objectives/components:1.Opportunities: Support African HEIs to be more visible and accessible, strengthen their profile, branding and disseminate targeted information, attract mobile learners, researchers and staff and sharing of data and information.HEIs will be supported in positioning themselves in fields in which they excel, and which can also highlight the linkages with EU investments at country or regional level. This positioning will help mobile learners, researchers and staff make informed decisions about their choice of studies, work and location and build up the internationalisation and marketing of countries offer. The lack of access to information and data is a significant barrier for mobile learners, researchers, HEIs in Africa and therefore SDG4 and SDG9, creating more inequalities in the continent and hampering mobility across the region.
